key_insight: Autocata turns catalyst screening into an autonomous, language-driven agent that maps high-level reaction goals to multistep reaction-network capabilities and executes the corresponding computational workflow.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce manual orchestration in catalyst discovery by automating model selection, candidate generation, validation, and ranking across complex reaction pathways.
method: Pretrains a Transformer on two million catalyst-adsorbate structures to learn catalytic representations.
Uses a capability registry of 79 adsorbate-specialized generative models covering C, N, O, and H reaction intermediates.
Decomposes natural-language prompts into reaction-network tasks, then configures generation, filtering, and ML-potential evaluation workflows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on CH4 activation, N2RR, and CO2-to-methanol pathways, showing end-to-end screening across multiple catalytic reaction networks.
watch_item: Performance depends on the coverage and correctness of the capability registry, so gaps in model specialization or reaction-network encoding could limit autonomy.
paper_title: Autocata: Reaction-network-guided autonomous catalyst screening via capability-centric AI
